notes.meaning: David cries out to God because the number of his enemies is growing fast. His own son Absalom has led a rebellion against him, and many former friends have joined the revolt. Instead of giving up in despair, David brings his sorrow directly to the Lord in prayer.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine interprets the psalm as the words of Christ, seeing the rising enemies as the crowds and Judas turning against Jesus during His passion.

notes.meaning: David's enemies mock him by claiming that God has abandoned him and will never rescue him. This cruel insult hurts him deeply, because his whole life is built on trusting the Lord. The word "Selah" invites the singer and listener to pause and think carefully about what was just said.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine explains that Christ's persecutors said there was no help for Him in God because they did not believe He would rise from the dead.

notes.meaning: David answers his enemies' taunts by declaring his complete confidence in God. He pictures the Lord as a shield surrounding him completely, keeping him safe from every attack. Even though David has fled his throne in deep shame, God is the One who restores his honor and lifts his head in hope.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine explains the lifter of the head as Christ's human mind remaining united to God throughout the shame and pain of the cross.

notes.meaning: David calls out loud to God in earnest prayer during his time of danger. Even though David had to leave Jerusalem, he knows the Lord still answers him from His holy hill. For God to hear His servant means He will surely act to deliver him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine teaches that this cry refers to the silent prayer of the heart rather than an outward spoken voice.

notes.meaning: David is able to lie down and sleep calmly, even with an army hunting him in the dark. He wakes up safe the next morning because the Lord sustains him, which means God supports and protects his life every moment. Peaceful rest is a gift from trusting that God never sleeps.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine interprets sleeping and waking as a prophecy of the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ.

notes.meaning: David declares that he will not give in to fear, even if tens of thousands of soldiers surround him on every side. Human numbers and military strength cannot stand against the almighty power of God. Knowing the Lord is with him gives David steady peace in the face of terrible odds.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine applies this verse to the hostile crowds that stood around Jesus at His crucifixion.

notes.meaning: David calls on God to take action right away and rescue him. He pictures his enemies as ferocious wild animals whose jawbones and teeth God shatters, making them completely unable to bite or harm him. Instead of seeking personal revenge, David leaves the battle and the punishment in the Lord's hands.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine sees the broken teeth as the silencing of the hateful accusations spoken against Christ.

notes.meaning: David finishes his song by giving all praise to the Lord, declaring that only God has the power to save. Deliverance from trouble does not come from human wisdom, armies, or schemes. David looks beyond his own needs and prays for God's goodness and favor to rest on all of His people.

differ.view: Teachers in this tradition emphasize this verse as proof that salvation is entirely God's work of sovereign grace alone, without any human contribution.
Teachers in this tradition emphasize that while God alone provides salvation through His mercy, believers must continually ask for and walk in His grace to remain under His blessing.
